paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus walks into the hardest night of His life with His eyes wide open. He says, "My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death." (Mark 14:34) He doesn't hide the weight, and He doesn't pretend it's small. He tells His Father all of it, and then He says, "Yet not what I will, but what You will." (Mark 14:36)

Now look at the three friends He asked to keep watch. Jesus says, "For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak." (Mark 14:38) And when the crowd comes and Jesus is seized, "everyone deserted Him and fled." (Mark 14:50) Friend, I've been the one who meant well and still came up short, so I'm not throwing stones. This passage tells us plainly that our best intentions run out, and that is exactly why Jesus says to "Watch and pray." (Mark 14:38)

And here's the part I want you to carry out of my bakery today. Jesus tells the crowd, "But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled." (Mark 14:49) Even with a kiss, a mob and an empty garden, God's plan is not slipping out of His hands. So when your own night feels heavy, pray the way Jesus did, honestly and all the way to the end: not my will, but Yours. The story isn't over, and Mark has more to tell us.
